title: The nonvanishing locus of an element of an invertible module over an affine scheme is affine
statement: Let R be a commutative ring and N an invertible R-module, meaning an R-module that is finite projective of rank 1 (equivalently, locally free of rank 1 on a cover of Spec(R) by standard opens D(f)). Let Sym_R(N) have canonical map iota as in [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-universal-property]. For s in N, let A=Sym_R(N) and B=A/(iota(s)-1)A. Then the morphism Spec(B) to Spec(R) [def-weil-affine-spectrum] identifies Spec(B) with the open subset V={p in Spec(R) | s is not in pN}; equivalently, V is affine.

proof.text: A finite projective module is finitely presented and its localization at every prime is finite free. Apply Module.FinitePresentation.exists_free_localizedModule_powers to the complement of each prime. It gives f outside that prime and a free N_f of the same finrank as N_p, namely 1. Module.nonempty_linearEquiv_of_finrank_eq_one supplies an explicit linear equivalence R_f ≃ N_f. These principal opens cover Spec R. The ULift ring equivalence transports the prime and the condition f outside it.

On a chosen chart put S=R_f, Q=B_(f), and a=e⁻¹(s/1). The canonical linear map j:N→Q sends s to 1. Extend j to the localized module, and let b be its value at the basis vector e(1). S-linearity gives a b=1, so a is invertible in Q. The localization universal property defines ψ:S_a→Q. In the opposite direction the R-linear functional n↦a⁻¹ e⁻¹(n/1) in S_a sends s to 1. Extend it using the symmetric-algebra universal property; quotient by (ι(s)-1), then invert f, to obtain φ:Q→S_a.

The map φ commutes with the maps from S, and ψ sends the inverse of a to b. Thus φψ is the identity by the localization universal property. For ψφ, precompose with B→Q, then with Sym_R(N)→B: the symmetric-algebra uniqueness reduces to degree-one generators. For each n, S-linearity gives j(n)=e⁻¹(n/1)b, which is exactly ψφ on that generator. The quotient and localization uniqueness now give ψφ=id. Hence Q is a principal localization of S at a. All maps and inverses are constructed explicitly; no unproved existence is used.

Transport the localization S=R_f along ULift.ringEquiv to S′=(ULift R)_(ULift f). IsLocalization.of_ringEquiv_left gives that Q is a principal localization of S′ at the transported coefficient. By IsOpenImmersion.of_isLocalization its spectrum map is an open immersion. SpecMapRestrictBasicOpenIso identifies that map with the restriction of the original morphism to D(ULift f). One application of IsZariskiLocalAtTarget.of_forall_exists_morphismRestrict, using the covering neighbourhoods from step 1, proves that the original morphism is an open immersion. This replaces fpqc descent by the proved Mathlib Zariski-local criterion.

For the image inclusion, let q be a prime of B and p its contraction. The map j:N→B has j(s)=1. Every element of p times N maps into q: on a generator r n, j(r n)=r j(n), and r maps into q. Thus s∈pN would imply 1∈q, a contradiction. This argument needs no rank or projectivity hypothesis.

For the reverse inclusion take s∉pN. Projectivity gives a splitting t:N→N→₀R of the canonical free-module surjection. If every coordinate of t(s) lay in p, the finite sum expression s=∑_n t(s)(n)n would put s in pN. Hence some coordinate linear functional l has l(s)∉p. In the residue field κ(p), normalize l by the inverse of its nonzero value on s. The resulting linear map sends s to 1 and therefore induces an R-algebra homomorphism B→κ(p) by the symmetric-algebra and quotient universal properties. Its kernel is prime, and its contraction is p because the structural map R→κ(p) has kernel p. This proves the reverse inclusion. Finally the ULift spectrum equivalence transports both inclusions to the statement as written.

proof_origin.note: Explicit universal-property proof of the chart localization, and direct projective-coordinate proof of the image equality; formalized entirely from Mathlib.
